newsitem.title: UK: CRICKET-MCGRATH MAKES UP FOR LOST TIME.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-MCGRATH MAKES UP FOR LOST TIME.

text.p: Glenn McGrath did his best to make up for lost time on Friday when the second Ashes test between England and Australia finally got underway at Lord's.
McGrath took three for 21 off 10 spiteful overs from the pavilion end to reduce England to 38 for three when rain stopped play half an hour before the scheduled lunch interval.

With only four days remaining in the match after rain had washed out play on Thursday's opening day, Mark Taylor had no hesitation in asking England to bat after winning the toss on a cool, cloudy morning.
The rangy McGrath fully vindicated his captain's decision by taking wickets with the final ball in each of his fourth, fifth and sixth overs from the pavilion end.

Mark Butcher, who had suffered a torrid time against Paul Reiffel moving the ball extravagantly off the seam from the Nursery end, was first to go, caught off a mixture of bat and pad at short-leg for five.

Michael Atherton, leading England for a record 42nd time, followed, caught at first slip by Taylor tumbling to his right for one and Alec Stewart was bowled, also for one, when he misjudged the line and offered no stroke to ball which clipped his off-stump.
Nasser Hussain and Graham Thorpe, England's batting heroes in the nine-wicket first test victory at Edgbaston, then dug in on a pitch offering plenty of assistance to the pace bowlers.
When lunch was taken 10 minutes early, Hussain was on 10 while Thorpe had scored 13.
